input: Build a simple wooden toolbox from scratch

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The size and capacity of the toolbox determines material quantities, cut dimensions, and structural requirements — a small hand-carry tote is very different from a large floor-standing chest.
Knowing who will use it (a child, a hobbyist, a professional tradesperson) shapes the ergonomics, durability requirements, and design complexity.
Where the build happens (garage workshop vs. apartment with basic tools) determines which joinery methods and power tools are feasible.
A budget limit drives wood species choice, hardware selection, and overall complexity — premium hardwood with metal fittings costs far more than basic pine.
Desired style and finish (rustic, painted, stained, natural) affects material choice, surface prep steps, and finishing products needed.
Knowing which tools the user already owns determines whether cuts, joints, and assembly steps need to be adapted to hand tools only or can use power tools.
Understanding what features define a successful result — a lid, a handle, interior dividers, portability — ensures the plan targets the right outcome.

gold.taskTitle: Build a simple wooden toolbox from scratch
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to design and construct a basic wooden toolbox, starting from raw materials with no pre-made kit.

questions.title: How large should the finished toolbox be?
questions.description: Should the toolbox be a small hand-carry tote, a medium bench-top box, or a larger floor-standing chest? This drives all cut dimensions and material quantities.

questions.title: Who is the toolbox primarily being built for?
questions.description: Is this for your own everyday use, a child, a hobbyist, or a professional tradesperson? The intended user shapes ergonomics and durability needs.

questions.title: What kind of workspace will you be building in?
questions.description: Do you have access to a full garage workshop, a small outdoor space, or just an apartment? This determines which cuts and joinery methods are realistic.

questions.title: What is your budget for materials and hardware?
questions.description: A rough budget range determines whether to use premium hardwood with metal fittings or keep it simple with basic pine and minimal hardware.

questions.title: What look or finish do you want on the toolbox?
questions.description: Are you aiming for a rustic, painted, stained, or natural wood finish? This affects wood species selection and the finishing steps in the plan.

questions.title: Which tools do you currently have available to build with?
questions.description: Do you own power tools like a circular saw and drill, or are you working with hand tools only? This shapes every joinery and assembly step in the plan.

questions.title: What specific features must the finished toolbox have?
questions.description: Does it need a hinged lid, a carrying handle, interior dividers, or tray inserts? Defining must-have features sets the target for what done looks like.
